svg.title: figure 8
svg.text: Why a leader only counts entries of its own term (Raft paper, Figure 8)
5 servers, log indices 1–3; colour = the term an entry was written in
copies t2 to S3: on 3 of 5!
(d) if S1 dies now: S5 wins t5
(e) safe path: S1 puts its t4
In (c) the t2 entry sits on a majority (S1, S2, S3), but it is NOT safe to call it committed:
S5's last entry is t3, newer than t2, so S2, S3 and S4 would all vote for S5 in term 5. S5 then overwrites index 2 → (d).
Raft's rule: the leader advances commit_index only to an index whose entry has the leader's CURRENT term.
In (e) the t4 entry is on S1, S2, S3. Now S5 (last t3) can't win, and committing index 3 commits index 2 with it.
Code: maybe_advance_commit stops at the first older-term entry (raft_node.cpp:258); become_leader appends a NOOP
so a new leader has a current-term entry at once (:248).
